source.title: Generalizable Video Quality Assessment via Weak-to-Strong Learning
source.authors: Lin-Han Cao; Wei Sun; Xiang-Yang Zhu; Kai-Wei Zhang; Jun Jia; Yicong Peng; Dandan Zhu; Guang-Tao Zhai; Xiong-Kuo Min

record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-to-strong training in video quality assessment, but uses VQA correlation metrics and a ranking-based setup rather than Burns et al.'s PGR measure. It is also an extension to a visual task.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own weak-teacher training results and method comparisons. The paper's cited summaries of prior weak-to-strong studies are not rows. Example prompts for the VQA model are not reviewer-directed instructions.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes a ~8B LMM student on pseudo-labels from five VQA teachers, without human labels, and compares it with each teacher on in-domain and OOD benchmarks. That is the naive weak-to-strong setup applied to a new task, video quality assessment. The measure is SRCC/PLCC, not PGR. It then tests training additions: ensembling, heterogeneous synthetic-distortion teachers, confidence loss and iterative self-teaching. T3 (new setting) fits better than T2, because the method is Burns-style naive fine-tuning plus known add-ons.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that naive W2S lets a strong LMM student match weak VQA teachers in-domain and surpass them out of distribution. They also conclude that ensembling, heterogeneous synthetic-distortion teachers, confidence loss and iterative self-teaching push the student past all teachers on ten benchmarks, reaching state of the art without human labels. Note that the teachers themselves were trained on human labels.
record.recipe_differences: The basic setup trains a stronger student on weak VQA supervision, but the task is video quality assessment and results are reported as SRCC/PLCC rather than PGR. The proposed enhanced method uses pairwise ranking, heterogeneous supervision, confidence loss, and iterative training.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by benchmark group, teacher, training-data scale, student backbone, and added training component; Table 2 reports a small in-domain decline after adding confidence loss but OOD gains.
record.code_released: https://github.com/clh124/W2S-VQA (the paper says data and code will be available)
record.problems: The paper does not calculate PGR, so its SRCC comparisons are not the claim's specified gap-recovered measure. The main aggregate results provide no uncertainty estimates. The study concerns one task domain, video quality assessment.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports per-dataset SRCC and PLCC values in Tables 2, 8, and 9, plus per-dataset method comparisons. To stay within the row limit, the extracted rows use the reported in-domain/OOD aggregates for these comparisons; the detailed per-dataset values and PLCC rows are not included.

untested.parts: PGR is never computed. A ground-truth-trained student exists (LSVQ-labeled, 27k), but it is trained on different data from the W2S students.
Components are added cumulatively and never ablated in isolation. Gains are over a ranking-based pipeline, not reported as PGR.
Student size is not varied (all students are 7-8B). There are no other tasks and no representation-based predictors. Only teacher strength and training-data scale vary.
Not tested: whether students exploit errors the teacher cannot check, and whether gains shrink when teacher and student err alike.
Only video quality assessment, with LMM students. No other vision tasks or pure vision models.

missing.what: Strong student trained on LSVQ ground-truth labels (27k): in-domain SRCC 0.851, OOD 0.577. This is the closest thing to a strong ceiling. It would give in-domain PGR near or below 0, and OOD PGR above 1 for the IX and Q-Align students.
Ablation of iterative Stage 2. Without difficult-sample selection, OOD SRCC is 0.669; without label refinement it is 0.657; full (V) is 0.722. Iteration gains vanish without these components.
Parameter counts: the Q-Align teacher has 8204M parameters vs the student's 8075M, so one 'weak' teacher is not smaller than the student.

record.verdict_notes: SRCC is used instead of PGR. 'Weak' teachers are state-of-the-art models, and Q-Align matches the student's size, so weakness is relative capability, not scale. No uncertainty is reported. All differences are small in-domain and could be noise. Tranche changed from T2 to T3. R31–R34 are moved from V3 to V2 because they compare method stages, not sizes.

versions.untested_parts: Does not calculate PGR or use Burns et al.'s gap-recovered measure.
Compares the stated ensemble, heterogeneous-supervision, confidence-loss, and iterative-training additions; does not compare other loss variants.
Tests VQA benchmarks, five teacher models, and three LMM student backbones, but does not calculate PGR or isolate representation properties as predictors.
Reports in-domain and OOD benchmark results, but does not test whether students exploit supervision errors the teacher cannot check, or whether gains shrink when teacher and student errors are alike.
No theoretical conditions for a student to outperform its supervisor are tested.
Tests video quality assessment, not other vision tasks or non-language modalities generally.

statements.correction: Table 1: LSVQ-ground-truth-trained student, 27k videos, SRCC 0.851 in-domain and 0.577 OOD. PGR is not reported explicitly.
statements.problem: The OOD comparisons are correct, but the assertion that no ground-truth-trained strong comparison exists is false.

statements.correction: Table 1 reports a student trained on 27k LSVQ ground-truth labels: in-domain SRCC 0.851, OOD SRCC 0.577. PGR can be calculated from these comparisons, although the paper does not report it.
statements.problem: The in-domain numbers and reported degradation are correct; the absence of a true-label comparison is incorrectly asserted.

statements.correction: Table 1: 27k LSVQ-ground-truth-trained student; SRCC 0.851 in-domain, 0.577 OOD. No corresponding 200k ground-truth-trained comparison is reported.
statements.problem: A ground-truth-trained strong student is tested in this paper.

statements.correction: Table 1, 27k videos: in-domain student-minus-teacher SRCC ranges from -0.004 to +0.002. Authors describe comparable performance; no uncertainty estimates are supplied.
statements.problem: The ±0.004 range is correct for 27k training videos; statistical noise is not established by reported uncertainty.

statements.correction: R21 and R23 concern VQA in-domain SRCC: homogeneous ensembling 0.849→0.856; heterogeneous supervision 0.856→0.858. Neither row shows reversal.
statements.problem: The statement contains no claim about this study, and its attached VQA rows do not support the listed task-specific reversals.
The OOD endpoints are correct; the claimed positive in-domain gain at every step omits the confidence-loss decrease.

statements.correction: Table 1: MinimalisticVQA(VII) teacher/student OOD SRCC 0.490/0.515; FAST-VQA 0.486/0.543. The stronger teacher in this comparison produces the weaker student. Section 4.1.2 describes the relationship as general.
statements.problem: The teacher/student values are correct, but the strength relationship is a general trend rather than a monotonic rule.

statements.correction: Table 1 supports a general association with exceptions: MinimalisticVQA(VII) teacher 0.490 exceeds FAST-VQA teacher 0.486, while their students score 0.515 and 0.543 respectively.
statements.problem: The reported verdict is paraphrased accurately, but its unqualified teacher-strength relationship overstates the table.
